extracted_factors.Label: Large-scale Oil Palm Plantations
extracted_factors.Description: Large-scale oil palm plantations are identified as a major driver of deforestation in Indonesia, contributing significantly to forest loss, particularly in the late 2000s.

extracted_factors.Label: Conversion to Grasslands
extracted_factors.Description: The conversion of forests to grasslands, often following fire activity, is noted as a significant driver of deforestation, particularly in certain years such as 2016.

extracted_factors.Label: Small-scale Agriculture
extracted_factors.Description: Small-scale agriculture and plantations are significant contributors to deforestation, especially outside major islands in Indonesia.

extracted_factors.Label: Logging Roads
extracted_factors.Description: Although declining, logging roads have been responsible for a portion of deforestation, suggesting a shift from selective logging to other types of activities.

extracted_factors.Label: Fire Activity
extracted_factors.Description: Periods of considerable fire activity have driven sharp rises in deforestation due to forest conversion to grasslands.

extracted_pain_points.description: A lack of information about the complex processes leading to deforestation limits effective forest conservation policy development.
Deforestation contributes to severe air pollution and public health crises due to the burning of organic peat soils.
Inadequate evaluation of the impacts of targeted forest conservation policies due to limited understanding of which drivers they counteract.
Drivers of deforestation exhibit significant spatial and temporal variation, requiring tailored policy interventions.
Sustainability standards are more difficult to enforce among small-scale plantation managers, posing challenges to monitoring deforestation.
